excerpts.text: In the school settings examined by the authors, shared instructional leadership was associated with stronger teacher collaboration. This observational finding does not establish causation or guarantee an outcome.
The authors recommend that school leaders make time for teachers to discuss instructional decisions.

Democracy concerns participation in collective decisions. Direct democracy involves citizens deciding issues themselves; representative democracy involves choosing people to decide on their behalf. This excerpt gives no account of institutions in ancient Athens.

learner_request: Explain what these sources support about leadership and direct democracy.

draft_blocks.text: In the schools described, shared instructional leadership was associated with stronger teacher collaboration. The observational finding does not establish causation.
Direct democracy means citizens decide issues themselves. These passages do not describe the institutions of ancient Athens.

For school leadership, the authors recommend making time for teachers to discuss instructional decisions. A suggested practice activity: outline an agenda for such a discussion. This activity is my adaptation.
